name: Chattoko: AI Live Chat & AI Receptionist
author: chattoko

sections.description:
Chattoko puts an AI on your website’s chat and, if you want it, on your business phone. You teach it with your own FAQs, documents and website, and it answers the questions you get every day. When a question needs a person, it hands the conversation to your team, with everything already in front of them.

This plugin is the connector between your WordPress site and your Chattoko account. A Chattoko account is required — the chat itself runs on the Chattoko service.

Want to see it first? Watch an install from start to finish, and read the steps with pictures.

On a WooCommerce store: the plugin, a read-only key, and the AI answering a shopper about colours and stock (Kiln & Linen is a made-up store; real Chattoko screens and AI answers).

What you get

  • An AI assistant trained on your own FAQs, documents and website content
  • Live chat with real-time typing indicators, then a clean handoff to a human agent
  • Proactive messages and chat flows — greet visitors, ask qualifying questions, capture leads
  • A shared inbox for your team, with tickets and email in the same place
  • Visitor context: which page they are on, device, approximate location
  • Customer satisfaction surveys after a chat
  • Available in 10 languages

AI receptionist, on Chat + Phone plans

The same AI answers your phone when you can’t.

  • It answers calls from your own FAQs and products, takes messages and booking requests, and puts the caller through to you when they need a person
  • Your team rings first. If nobody picks up, or it’s after hours, the AI answers
  • Forward the number you have to your Chattoko number, or get a new local number in Australia, the US or Canada
  • Calls the AI handles are written out, and recorded calls get a summary

The plugin adds the chat to your site. The phone is set up in your Chattoko dashboard.

Plans and trial

Every plan starts with a 14-day trial, and the trial needs a card. Nothing is charged for 14 days: cancel in Settings → Billing & Plans before day 14 and you pay nothing. Chat plans start at US$59 a month. Chat + Phone plans, with calls, SMS and the AI receptionist, start at US$139 a month. Current prices are on https://chattoko.io/pricing. The plugin itself is free and has no locked features: everything you pay for runs on the Chattoko service.

WooCommerce live chat and chatbot

If WooCommerce is active, the plugin reports the visitor’s cart value, currency and item count to the widget, not which products are in the cart. That lets your chat flows react to the cart — for example, offer help when a cart passes a value you choose, or greet someone who has just added an item. You can turn this off in the plugin settings.

The cart is read in the visitor’s browser from WooCommerce’s own Store API (/wp-json/wc/store/v1/cart), and read again when an item is added, so AJAX add-to-cart works without a page reload. Nothing visitor-specific is printed into your pages, so page caching stays safe.

Separately, connect your store in the Chattoko dashboard (Integrations → WooCommerce, with a read-only REST API key) and Chattoko becomes a WooCommerce chatbot that knows your shop: the AI answers from your published products, with their prices, sizes, colours and stock, and your team sees a customer’s WooCommerce orders beside their chat. A chat flow can look up an order by its number for a customer who gives the email or phone on it. The AI taking orders, in chat and on calls (checkout links and draft orders with Shopify, pickup orders paid on Square), and looking an order up itself work with Shopify or Square stores, not WooCommerce. See what works with WooCommerce.

Setup

  1. Install and activate the plugin
  2. Open Chattoko in the admin menu and paste your Workspace ID from your Chattoko dashboard
  3. Save — the widget appears on your site

External services

This plugin connects your site to Chattoko, a hosted live chat service operated by Chattoko (https://chattoko.io). The plugin is a connector; the chat service itself runs on Chattoko’s servers, and a Chattoko account is required to use it.

What the plugin loads

Once you save a Workspace ID, the plugin loads the chat widget script from https://chattoko.io/widget/widget.js on your site’s front end, and adds the Workspace ID to your pages as a <meta name="chattoko-workspace"> tag so the widget can find it. Before a Workspace ID is saved, the plugin loads nothing and contacts no external server.

What the settings page checks

When an administrator opens the Chattoko settings page with a Workspace ID saved, your WordPress server reads that workspace’s public chat settings from firestore.googleapis.com (Chattoko’s database, Firebase Firestore on Google Cloud). These are the same settings the widget reads in a visitor’s browser: the business name and whether the chat may show. Only the Workspace ID is sent, under the plugin’s own name (Chattoko-WordPress) rather than your site’s address, and as with any web request your server’s IP address reaches Google. The answer is used to show the workspace’s name, or why the chat is not showing, and is not stored.

Which servers the widget talks to

Chattoko’s backend runs on Google Cloud, so once the widget is running in a visitor’s browser it contacts these hosts directly. They are all part of the Chattoko service:

  • chattoko.io — the widget script itself, and anonymous counts of how visitors use the chat button and greeting: shown, opened or dismissed (chattoko.io/w/ev)
  • identitytoolkit.googleapis.com and securetoken.googleapis.com — Firebase Authentication, used to give the visitor an anonymous identity so their conversation can be theirs alone. The second host renews that identity when a visitor comes back later
  • firestore.googleapis.com — Firebase Firestore, the live database that carries the conversation between the visitor and your agents
  • firebasestorage.googleapis.com — Firebase Storage: your business logo in the chat window on every page where the widget loads, and any file or image attached to a chat
  • australia-southeast1-chat-app-b5947.cloudfunctions.net — Chattoko’s backend functions on Google Cloud Functions, contacted only when a visitor asks for a copy of the conversation by email, confirms their phone number with a code, or opens a link that continues a conversation started by text message
  • www.google.com, www.gstatic.com and content-firebaseappcheck.googleapis.com — Google reCAPTCHA Enterprise and Firebase App Check, which protect the chat from automated abuse. reCAPTCHA looks at how the page is used in the visitor’s browser and sends that to Google to tell people from bots. Its use is subject to the Google Privacy Policy (https://policies.google.com/privacy) and Terms of Service (https://policies.google.com/terms)
  • fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com — Google Fonts, for the widget’s typeface

Google Fonts and reCAPTCHA both run in the visitor’s browser and reach Google directly, so the visitor’s IP address reaches Google. Some jurisdictions treat that as needing consent. If that applies to you, take it into account before enabling the widget.

What is sent to Chattoko, and when

The widget runs in your visitors’ browsers and sends data to Chattoko’s servers:

  • On every page where the widget loads: the page URL and title, referrer, browser and device type, language, and an approximate location derived from the visitor’s IP address. A first-party identifier is stored in the browser so a returning visitor’s conversation continues.
  • When a visitor opens the chat and writes: their messages, and any name, email address or phone number they choose to provide.
  • If the WooCommerce option is enabled: the value of the items in the cart (with tax and discounts, without shipping), the currency and the number of items, read from your own store’s Store API in the visitor’s browser and passed to the widget when a page loads and when the cart changes.

This data is processed by Chattoko to deliver the chat service — showing the conversation to your agents, generating AI replies, and producing your analytics.

Terms and privacy

  • Terms of Service: https://chattoko.io/terms
  • Privacy Policy: https://chattoko.io/privacy

Because the widget collects visitor data, review your own site’s privacy policy and any consent requirements that apply to you before enabling it.
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin through Plugins → Add Plugin, or upload the chattoko folder to /wp-content/plugins/
  2. Activate it through the Plugins menu
  3. Open Chattoko in the admin menu (the same page is also under Settings → Chattoko)
  4. Paste your Workspace ID and save

You will find your Workspace ID in the Chattoko dashboard under Settings → Installation. No account yet? Sign up at https://chattoko.io/signup?via=wordpress and start a 14-day trial. The trial needs a card, and nothing is charged for 14 days.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Chattoko account?

Yes. This plugin connects your WordPress site to the Chattoko service — the chat, the AI and your team inbox all live there. You can create an account at https://chattoko.io/signup?via=wordpress.

Where do I find my Workspace ID?

Log in to your Chattoko dashboard, go to Settings → Installation, and copy the ID under Your workspace ID. It is 6 to 64 letters, numbers, dashes or underscores. If you paste something else, the plugin keeps the ID you had and tells you why. Once an ID is saved, the page shows your workspace’s name, or why the chat is not showing yet: no plan chosen, live chat switched off, or no workspace with that ID.

How much does Chattoko cost?

Every plan starts with a 14-day trial, and the trial needs a card. Nothing is charged for 14 days, and if you cancel before day 14 you pay nothing. Chat plans start at US$59 a month, and Chat + Phone plans, with calls, SMS and the AI receptionist, at US$139 a month. Current prices are on https://chattoko.io/pricing.

Can the AI answer my phone too?

Yes, on a Chat + Phone plan. Forward the number you have to your Chattoko number, or get a new local number in Australia, the US or Canada. Your team rings first, and the AI answers when nobody picks up or after hours. The phone is set up in your Chattoko dashboard; the plugin only adds the chat to your site.

Does the widget slow my site down?

The widget script is loaded with defer, so it never blocks your page from rendering. It is served from a CDN and loads after your content.

Does it work with WooCommerce?

Yes. When WooCommerce is active, the plugin reports the cart’s value, currency and item count, so your chat flows can react to the cart. It can be switched off in the plugin settings. Connect the store under Integrations → WooCommerce in your Chattoko dashboard and the AI also answers from your products, your team sees a customer’s orders beside their chat, and a chat flow can look up an order by its number.

Does it work with caching and optimisation plugins?

Yes. Nothing visitor-specific is printed into your pages, so full-page caching is safe. The Workspace ID is also printed as a meta tag, so the chat keeps working when an optimisation plugin combines or delays scripts. We tested Autoptimize and LiteSpeed Cache, including LiteSpeed’s “Combine External and Inline JS”. If you combine scripts, the bundled copy of the widget only updates when your cache is cleared, so excluding chattoko.io/widget from JS combining keeps you on the latest version.

What happens if I deactivate the plugin?

The widget stops loading immediately. Your Workspace ID is kept so you can reactivate without setting it up again — deleting the plugin removes it.

Is my visitors’ data sent to a third party?

Yes — the chat service is hosted by Chattoko. The “External services” section above lists exactly what is sent and when, and links to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.
sections.changelog:
1.0.2

  • Fixed: the settings page now says what the chat sends on every page where it loads (the page address and title, where the visitor came from, browser and device type, language and approximate location), not only when someone opens the chat. This readme already said so.
  • Changed: the WooCommerce option says what it sends: the cart’s value and how many items are in it, not which products.

1.0.1

  • Changed: the plugin is now called Chattoko: AI Live Chat & AI Receptionist. Its folder and settings are the same.
  • New: a Chattoko menu in the admin sidebar. Settings → Chattoko still opens the same page.
  • New: the settings page checks the Workspace ID with Chattoko and shows the workspace’s name, or why the chat is not showing. It used to say “Connected” for any ID of the right shape.
  • New: until a Workspace ID is saved, administrators see one notice with a button to the Chattoko page. It can be dismissed, and it goes away once the chat is on.
  • Changed: the sign-up links open Chattoko’s sign-up with WordPress already chosen as your platform.

1.0.0

  • Initial release
